result:
I've written and run the A17 acceptance suites. They exposed **three product defects**, so two of the six acceptance items are not met: the full `tests/qa` run and the e2e run both exit 1. I kept the failing tests and didn't work around any defect. Everything is uncommitted on `dg6/qa-a`; `HEAD` is still `772bda86b`. The DG5 historical validator passed (exit 0) at the start and at the end.

**Results**

| Check | Exit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Full `tests/qa` integration run | 1 | 33 files, 348 passed, 2 failed (F1 and F2, both in my A17 file); every other QA suite passes |
| Root e2e, chromium-en and chromium-ar | 1 | 8 passed, 2 failed (the signed webhook in both languages, F1); axe found 0 serious or critical issues on every screen it reached |
| `pnpm lint` and prettier check | 0 | clean |
| REQ-S01-005 suite | 0 | 4/4 pass |
| Mutation checks | n/a | 7 central assertions killed (one or more per scenario); 1 survived, disclosed below |

- **8/1/1 import, CSV and XLSX:** passes in the API suite and in e2e. 8 KPI actuals are committed, each with lineage to its batch and source row. The invalid and duplicate rows stay visible with their reasons. Re-importing commits nothing, and a commit whose rows became invalid writes nothing at all.
- **Webhooks:** unsigned, wrongly signed, tampered and stale deliveries all get 401 and store nothing. A correctly signed delivery also gets 401 (F1).
- **Failing and stopped connectors:**
  - The connector page shows which run failed, why, what to do, and both fallbacks.
  - Each connector's failure produces exactly one exception.
  - The stale KPI keeps its last value and date, and no data changes.
  - With the connector stopped, the form and file import still work.
  - The only failure is the exception's missing KPI link (F2).

**Findings** (IDs are proposals for the orchestrator)
- **F-DG6-QA-A-1, High, breaks a mandatory requirement (REQ-S17-003): every correctly signed webhook is refused with 401.** `server.ts` creates the secret registry but never hands it to the integrations module; `setConnectorSecretProviders` is called only in tests. Connector credential references can't resolve either. The real server logs `secret_unresolvable` even with the variable set. Adding that one call in a sandbox copy makes both webhook tests pass.
- **F-DG6-QA-A-2, Medium (REQ-S12-019): a connector's operational exception never lists the affected KPI.** The worker raises it without KPI links, so `linkedKpis` is `[]`. Because of the scope rules, transformation-scoped data owners probably can't see these exceptions either; I inferred that from the scope rule and didn't test it.
- **F-DG6-QA-A-3, Medium: the webhook item keys are documented wrongly.** ADR-0056 §7 shows camelCase keys, the server only accepts the template's snake_case column keys (400 otherwise), and OpenAPI documents neither. My suite sends the template's column keys.

**Disclosures**
- **Survived mutation:** one mutation survived because F1 makes the signature comparison unreachable. A reachable variant (accept any signature) is killed.
- **Disk incident:** my first mutation sandbox was a full clone (3.7 GB). It briefly dropped free space on the shared `/var/tmp` to 2.0 GB, under the 3 GB floor. I deleted it within a minute and used a 19 MB minimal copy instead; free space stayed at or above 5.1 GB after that.
- **My own test bugs, fixed and logged:** an earlier full run and two earlier e2e runs failed partly because of mistakes in my tests (wrong KPI panel period, a scoping error, a page limit). Those logs are kept and explained in the handback.
- **Vitest config loader:** `node_modules` is read-only in this worktree, so Vitest runs with `--configLoader runner`, as a DG5 handback did.
- **e2e prerequisite:** the e2e spec needs `QA_A17_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET` (any synthetic value) exported before `with-stack.sh`.

**Not covered**
- REQ-S19-007, a DG7 handover row.
- A succeeded run's counts and last-success date on the connector page; these are proven through the API only.
- The exception screen in e2e: the stack script starts no worker, so no exception exists there. It is proven in the API suite with the real worker.

**Files written** (all new):
- `tests/qa/support/a17-files.ts`
- `tests/qa/support/a17.ts`
- `tests/qa/integration/a17-import-and-integration.test.ts`
- `tests/qa/integration/a17-s01-005-external-change.test.ts`
- `e2e/a17-import-and-integration.spec.ts`

The handback, with the requirement → test table, exact requests and responses for each defect, the mutation table and per-file counts, is in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/qa/T-DG6-QA-A-authoring/`, together with all logs and screenshots. Open `handback.md` first.
